name: gev_fly_to_location
description: [God's Eye View] Fly the God's Eye View camera to a known city, geocoded country/region/city/landmark, or explicit WGS84 coordinate. Countries/cities frame the whole place; landmarks/buildings use close framing.

locationId.description: Known city preset ID. Use when the requested place matches one of these cities.

query.description: Plain place search query, e.g. "London", "Eiffel Tower", or "Dubai Marina".

viewMode.description: Optional framing intent. Usually omit this; GEV infers whole-place framing for countries/cities and close framing for landmarks.

rangeM.description: Optional camera range from the target in meters. Omit it for automatic whole-country/whole-city or close-landmark framing; provide it only when the user explicitly requests a numeric height or distance.

waitForArrival.description: Set true when a later tool depends on the destination viewport. The result then waits for the camera flight and returns arrived=true; cancellation returns ok=false.

name: gev_select_nearest_aircraft
description: [God's Eye View] Atomically fly to a place, wait for arrival, enable and load Flights or Military Flights in that viewport, exclude on-ground records, and select/follow the nearest airborne aircraft. Healthy fallback feeds remain usable and are reported in the result. This does not open Contacts or Cockpit.

layerId.description: Aircraft layer to enable and search. Use flights unless the user explicitly asks for military aircraft.

locationId.description: Known city preset ID when the place matches one of these cities.

locationQuery.description: Free-form destination when no locationId matches.

name: gev_adjust_camera_zoom
description: [God's Eye View] Move the current Cesium camera closer to or farther from what it is presently looking at. Use for relative zoom requests without changing location.

amount.description: Use little for phrases like "a bit" or "a little", medium for ordinary zoom requests, and lot for "way out/in".

name: gev_zoom_to_globe
description: [God's Eye View] Pull the camera out to an ABSOLUTE full-Earth globe view (~18,000 km altitude, the whole planet in frame), keeping the current region centered. Use for "globe view", "whole earth", "see the planet", "zoom all the way out". Never use adjust_camera_zoom for these — its relative steps cannot reach the globe.

name: gev_set_layer_visibility
description: [God's Eye View] Enable or disable one registered God's Eye View data layer.

layerId.description: Common-name mapping for the non-obvious ids: space mission(s) → rocket-launches; fires/wildfires/active fires → local-firms (NASA FIRMS); ships/vessels/boats → ais-live-vessels; undersea/submarine cables → telegeography-submarine-cables; datacenters → local-datacenters; dams → local-dams; bikes/bike share → bikeshare; street traffic/congestion → traffic; traffic cameras → cctv; internet radio/stations → radio; ALPR/license plate readers/Flock cameras → alpr-cameras.

name: gev_show_data_layers_menu
description: [God's Eye View] Open the data layers dropdown/menu and optionally scroll to a specific layer row without toggling it.

layerId.description: Optional layer row to scroll into view and highlight.

name: gev_set_panel_open
description: [God's Eye View] Open or close a GEV UI panel/dropdown.

name: gev_set_context_mode
description: [God's Eye View] Enter or exit the Global Context sub-mode used by Contacts and Space Missions. Use Contacts only when the user explicitly requests Contacts, and Space Missions only when explicitly requested. A request to open the parent Context panel alone uses set_panel_open and must not activate either sub-mode. Selecting an aircraft does not imply Context.

mode.description: Use off to exit context mode.

name: gev_control_cockpit
description: [God's Eye View] Read or control Cockpit when the user explicitly requests Cockpit: establish Contacts and enter from a selected or tracked aircraft; exit; or navigate nearby Contacts with optional filters. Selecting or viewing an aircraft alone must not enter Cockpit.

action.description: previous/next (or prev) navigates through nearby contacts in Cockpit context.

targetLayer.description: Optional contact layer filter for next/previous (for example military for a military-only cycle).

aircraftClass.description: Optional aircraft class filter (for example helicopter) when using next/previous navigation.

name: gev_set_visual_style
description: [God's Eye View] Set the active God's Eye View visual filter/style.

name: gev_get_entity_context
description: [God's Eye View] Get current GEV scene context, including basemap/3D-tile target context, selected entity metadata if active, and entities currently visible in the camera view.

scope.description: Use auto by default. selected returns the clicked/selected entity; in_view returns visible entities near the screen center.

layerId.description: Optional layer filter for visible entity context.

name: gev_get_current_view_state
description: [God's Eye View] Read the current camera, style, Context, Cockpit, HUD, detection, map stack, post-processing, scene-playback, tracked-entity, and layer state before choosing another action.

name: gev_set_hud
description: [God's Eye View] Control the intelligence HUD overlay: visibility and/or layout variant.

name: gev_set_detection
description: [God's Eye View] Control the detection overlay: on/off, density-derived Sparse/Balanced/Dense profile, and Elastic/Weighted layer allocation.

enabled.description: false turns detection OFF; true restores the current density-derived profile.

densityPct.description: Density snaps to 0, 25, 50, 75, or 100 and derives the active profile.

allocationStrategy.description: Elastic splits evenly then lends unused slots; Weighted follows demand and semantic weight.

name: gev_set_map_stack
description: [God's Eye View] Switch the basemap/imagery stack (NOT the satellites data layer and NOT a visual style filter).

stack.description: photoreal = Google 3D. Use bing-aerial only when the user explicitly says "Bing aerial" — "satellite(s)" never means a basemap; only the explicit phrase "Esri" / "Esri imagery" means esri-imagery.

name: gev_set_post_processing
description: [God's Eye View] Control bloom and sharpen post-processing toggles and intensities.

name: gev_control_scene
description: [God's Eye View] Cinematic scene playback: list scenes, play one scene by name, stop, advance, or read status. Play starts a single named scene and returns immediately.

sceneId.description: Scene id or (partial) title for play.

name: gev_control_cctv
description: [God's Eye View] CCTV camera operations: enable/disable the layer, select a camera by name, next/prev/nearest/focus, toggle coverage wedges / projection overlay / auto-hop, "viewshed" for color-coded per-camera coverage volumes, and "adjust" for the on-camera calibration gizmo.

cameraQuery.description: Camera name or id for select.

enabled.description: Explicit on/off for coverage/viewshed/adjust/projection/autohop; omit to toggle.

name: gev_control_radio
description: [God's Eye View] Control Internet Radio playback without moving the map. Use select whenever the request includes a station category, name, country, coordinates, or nearby place—even when the user says play. Use play only for an unqualified "turn on/start the radio" request so the current or nearest station begins. Enable only reveals the Radio layer/markers without audio. Also supports disable, resume, pause, stop, next/previous, volume, and status.

action.description: Use select for any request qualified by category, station, country, coordinates, or place. Use play only for an unqualified turn on/start/listen request. Use enable only when the user explicitly asks to show or enable the Radio layer or its markers without requesting audio.

volumePct.description: Required for volume; sets the persistent Radio playback volume.

category.description: Station category for select/next/previous. When the user requests playback with a category, action must be select, not play.

locationQuery.description: Place to search near, such as "Austin, Texas" or "Seattle". Selection does not fly the camera.

country.description: Country code or name filter, for example US or United States.

name: gev_track_entity
description: [God's Eye View] Find and follow a specific aircraft (callsign/ICAO hex), ship (name/MMSI), or satellite (name/NORAD id) on enabled layers. Camera follows the entity.

query.description: Callsign, ship name, satellite name, ICAO hex, MMSI, or NORAD id.

layerId.description: Optional layer hint: flights | military | ais-live-vessels | satellites.

name: gev_stop_tracking
description: [God's Eye View] Stop following the tracked aircraft/satellite and clear any selected vessel.

name: gev_frame_overhead
description: [God's Eye View] Cinematically frame entities near the current view: pulls the camera back and angles it so nearby aircraft, ships, or satellites are visible together.

radiusKm.description: Search radius around the view target. Defaults: 150 aircraft, 120 ships, 3000 satellites.

name: gev_annotate_map
description: [God's Eye View] Draw annotations on the 3D map to visually point out what you are talking about — like sketching on a whiteboard over the world. Use this whenever you mention a specific place, building, campus, boundary, district, or a relationship between two places, so the user can SEE what you mean. Give place NAMES (preferred) or explicit lat/lng; the app resolves them to real-world positions and real building/area outlines — never guess pixel positions. Call this as you begin describing something, and you may mark several places in one call.

annotations.description: One or more things to mark. Mark multiple related places together when describing them as a group.

type.description: pin = planted marker at a spot; highlight = pulsing ring drawing the eye to a point; area = trace the outline of a building/campus/compound/district; arrow = a connector from one place to another (use target as the origin and toTarget as the destination); route = a path through several waypoints (use the points array); label = a floating text callout.

target.description: Place name to resolve, e.g. "Palace of Fine Arts, San Francisco", "the Pentagon", "Presidio of San Francisco". Preferred over coordinates. For a specific monument/statue/feature that sits within a larger landmark, use its OWN name + city ("Tejano Monument, Austin", "Texas African American History Memorial, Austin") — do NOT phrase it as "X at the Texas State Capitol", which makes the geocoder collapse several of them onto the same centroid so they stack on one spot.

points.description: For type=route: 2+ ordered waypoints the path passes through, each a place name (or coordinates / screen point).

mode.description: For type=route: travel mode for a real street-following route (the app returns distance + time). Pick from the verb the user used ("walk" → walking, "drive" → driving). Defaults to walking.

latitude.description: Explicit latitude (use only if no good place name exists).

toTarget.description: For type=arrow: the destination place name.

label.description: Short caption shown on the map (a few words). Optional.

color.description: Accent color. primary = neutral, amber = point of interest, cyan = infrastructure, green = confirmed/safe, red = alert.

footprint.description: For type=area/highlight: trace the real building or campus outline from map data. Defaults true for area.

intent.description: For type=area: "the_thing" (default) outlines the place itself (its footprint/boundary); "around_the_thing" highlights a surrounding zone (a buffered radius around it). Infer from phrasing: "the Capitol"/"show me X" → the_thing; "around/near/by X" or "the area around X" → around_the_thing.

entityKind.description: What KIND of thing the target IS — a fact, not a style choice: building = one structure; compound = campus/grounds/mall/park; district = neighborhood or area of a city; street = a named road/corridor; point_feature = monument/statue/memorial/plaque/fountain or other small point landmark. Set it whenever you know it — it routes the resolver to the right footprint source (point_feature anchors monuments as precise points instead of adopting a nearby building outline).

screenX.description: Fallback only: when you cannot name/geocode the place but can SEE it in the latest viewport screenshot, the normalized horizontal position (0=left, 1=right) of the spot. The app converts it back to a real world point under that pixel.

screenY.description: Fallback only: normalized vertical position (0=top, 1=bottom) of the spot in the latest viewport screenshot.

toScreenX.description: For type=arrow: normalized x of the arrow destination from the screenshot (pixel fallback).

toScreenY.description: For type=arrow: normalized y of the arrow destination from the screenshot (pixel fallback).

flyTo.description: Also move the camera to frame the first annotation. Default false — leave false if the user is already looking at the spot.

persist.description: Keep annotations until cleared (true, default) or let them auto-fade after ~20s (false).

name: gev_clear_annotations
description: [God's Eye View] Erase ALL map annotations previously drawn with annotate_map. Call this ONLY when the user EXPLICITLY asks to clear or reset the map. Annotations accumulate and persist across navigation and topic changes by design — never clear on your own initiative.

name: gev_move_camera
description: [God's Eye View] Direct the camera like a drone operator: orbit the current view target, pan, tilt, or rotate — one bounded nudge (mode=once) or continuous motion until stopped (mode=continuous). Continuous motion also stops on any manual camera input or when a navigation tool runs. Say the RESULTING state when confirming ("Orbiting slowly").

direction.description: Required except for orbit (defaults right/clockwise) and stop.

mode.description: once = bounded eased nudge (default); continuous = until stop/manual input.

name: gev_fly_route
description: [God's Eye View] Cinematic dolly along an EXISTING route annotation (drawn earlier with annotate_map type=route) — flies the street-following path from start to end. Omit label for the newest route. If no route is drawn, this fails with guidance: draw the route first.

label.description: Match an existing route mark by (partial) label.

name: gev_analyst_query
description: [God's Eye View] Answer questions ABOUT the data currently loaded on the map — counts, lists, superlatives, and attribute filters over live layers (flights, military, ships, fires, earthquakes). Examples: "how many flights over Texas", "biggest fire near LA", "which ships are headed to Oakland", "anything above 40,000 feet", "fastest thing in view". Queries ONLY client-side data from ENABLED layers — if the needed layer is off, say so and offer to enable it. For a follow-up about the previous answer's set ("which of those is closest?"), set followUp=true and send only the new filters/sort.

layers.description: Layers to query. fires/wildfires → local-firms; ships/vessels → ais-live-vessels.

scope.description: Spatial scope. Default: view (near the camera). Use kind=region for "over Texas"-style asks; kind=anywhere for global questions.

name.description: For kind=region: a state/country ("Texas", "France") or a named natural region ("the Alps", "Gulf of Mexico").

filters.description: Attribute predicates, ANDed. ALTITUDE IS METERS (40,000 ft = 12192). Fields: altitudeM, speedMps, military, onGround, aircraftClass, callsign, operator, routeOrigin, routeDestination, originCountry (flights); speedKts, shipType, destination (ships); frp, confidence (fires); magnitude, depthKm, place (earthquakes).

sortBy.description: Field to rank by, or "distance" for nearest-first.

followUp.description: true = re-query the PREVIOUS result set instead of fresh data.

name: gev_next_iss_pass
description: [God's Eye View] When the user asks when the ISS / the space station will next fly over: returns the next visible ISS pass for the current camera location (or an explicit lat/lon) — rise time (ISO + minutes from now), rise compass direction, peak elevation, and duration. Requires the satellites layer to have loaded its catalog at least once this session; if it hasn't, tell the user to enable the satellites layer and try again.

latitude.description: Optional observer latitude. Omit to use the current camera position.

longitude.description: Optional observer longitude. Omit to use the current camera position.

minElevationDeg.description: Minimum peak elevation (deg) to count as a pass. Default 10.
